title: NISA (Nippon Individual Savings Account)
subtitle: New NISA starting from 2024
description: NISA is a tax-exempt investment system where investment gains are not taxed.

tsumitate.title: Tsumitate Investment Allowance
tsumitate.description: Investment trusts suitable for long-term, regular, and diversified investment

lifetime.title: Tax-exempt Holding Limit
lifetime.description: Up to 12 million yen for Growth Investment Allowance

unlimited.title: Unlimited Tax-exempt Period
unlimited.description: Holdings remain tax-exempt as long as they are not sold

reusable.title: Reusable Allowance
reusable.description: Sold portions of the allowance can be reused from the following year

combined.title: Combined Use
combined.description: Tsumitate and Growth Investment Allowances can be used together

tsumitate.title: Tsumitate Investment Allowance
items: Low-cost products suitable for long-term investment

items.question: Can I have multiple NISA accounts?
items.answer: No, each person can only have one NISA account. However, you can change financial institutions on a yearly basis.

items.question: Can I buy foreign stocks with NISA?
items.answer: Yes, you can purchase foreign listed stocks and ETFs with the Growth Investment Allowance. However, availability varies by securities company.

items.question: Are dividends also tax-exempt?
items.answer: Yes, dividends from stocks held in a NISA account are also tax-exempt. However, they may be taxed depending on the dividend receiving method.

disclaimer: * This information is for reference only. Please confirm details with the FSA or your securities company.
